name: Baglioni Resort Cala del Porto
insider_take: This Tuscan coastal gem sits on a private peninsula where medieval watchtowers once guarded against pirates, now offering guests panoramic views of crystal-clear waters and the exclusive Argentario archipelago.
whats_special: Built on the historic Punta Ala promontory, this resort occupies land once owned by Italian nobility and features its own private beach club. The property's unique position offers direct access to some of Tuscany's most pristine sailing waters, while the nearby Uccellina Natural Park protects wild boar, deer, and over 200 bird species.
pro_tip: Book a sunset sailing excursion to the exclusive Giannutri Island - the resort's concierge can arrange private yacht access to this protected marine sanctuary that's typically off-limits to large tour groups.
dont_miss: The resort's signature aperitivo experience at Torre di Punta Ala, a 16th-century watchtower converted into an intimate cocktail venue. Time it perfectly with golden hour for Instagram-worthy shots of the Tyrrhenian Sea stretching toward Corsica on clear days.
pros: Stunning beachfront location with private access to pristine Mediterranean waters
Elegant Italian luxury design with sophisticated Tuscan coastal ambiance
World-class spa and wellness facilities with panoramic sea views
Exceptional gourmet dining featuring local Tuscan and Mediterranean cuisine
cons: Secluded Punta Ala location requires planning for exploring nearby attractions
Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive resort positioning
